issues.text: О1 — the single source of the floor value and who raises it. Default (criterion 1 is written with it): `engines.node` of tools/package.json is the source; the version rule of tools/src holds the value once, hook.sh once, the README Node line once, and a test of criterion 1 proves that they all equal engines (a copy at 22.23.3 is red); at each Node 22 security release ORCH opens a defect that raises every place in one run (decisions/0101: 'repeated at each Node security release'), and the owner is told in the report. Alternative: the guards read package.json at run time (no copies to drift, but every start reads and parses a file, and hook.sh cannot easily). Proposal: ORCH records the choice (Q12) before the design.

О2 — engine-strict. Default: no tools/.npmrc; engines stays declarative and the refusal lives in the runtime guards (trial E: `npm run` runs on 22.21.1 even with --engine-strict). Alternative: `engine-strict=true` in tools/.npmrc makes `npm ci` refuse below the floor (trial E: exit 1 under 22.21.1 and 22.23.3, 0 under 22.23.4), a second wall at step 3 of check.yml and in REQ-002's clean-copy check; its cost: the engines of every development dependency become hard too. No test names an .npmrc today. The design may propose it with its own test.

О3 — the hook's rule for a node-path binary below the floor. Default (criterion 4 (b) is written with it): fall through — the node-path binary gets the same `--version` check as the PATH node and the fallbacks; a candidate below the floor is skipped for the next one in the order node-path, PATH, SAI_NODE_FALLBACKS; with none left the hook ends with code 0, quietly, and the event is lost, never written later (R2). Alternative: stop at once when node-path names a below-floor binary — it loses events while a good Node is on the computer, against REQ-001 criterion 15 («записывает событие … если Node 22 на компьютере есть»). The diagnosis's mutant F11 assumes the fall-through.

О4 — how CI is bound to the floor. Default (criterion 8): `check-latest: true` on the setup-node step beside `node-version: "22"`, so the runner takes the newest 22.x of the manifest instead of its cache; trial T2: CI-1…CI-8 stay green (26 of 26), which also means no rule sees it today, so criterion 8 asks for a CI-3 rule row and a red damaged copy without it; plus the guards, which make any run below the floor red (criteria 5, 6). Alternative: node-version as a range `>=22.23.4 <23` (trial T3: CI-3 and CI-8 red, the table changes the node-version rule; a cached older patch above the floor may still be used). The setup-node action is pinned to a commit (CI-5), so its log line `node: v…` keeps its form until the pin changes.

О5 — the scope of the commands. Settled, not a question: DEP-01 and DEP-02 are closed together (decisions/0101 Addition, the defect). Open: (a) tools/src/pixel-office/public/office-report.js, a Node program a person starts for the UAT of REQ-001 (design 3.8), reads only — not in the diagnosis's list (its I10); default: included (criterion 5); (b) `npm test`, `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check` themselves are not guarded (Node's runner and the development tools; criterion 6 makes `npm run check` stop at `npm run traces`); default: not guarded, named in «Not covered»; (c) the stand-ins under tools/test/fixtures: out of scope; (d) .githooks/pre-push runs `npm run check` and inherits its refusal: no change.

О6 — documents. Default (criterion 9): tools/README.md lines 157 and 207, which say how hook.sh looks for and finds 'Node 22', join the write set: with the hook rule they turn false, and no test pins them (the diagnosis's I6). PLAN M0.9 says 'tools/README.md line 9 only (never line 176: DC-01)'; that wording protects line 176, which stays byte for byte. If ORCH keeps 'line 9 only', the second part of criterion 9 needs a micro-amendment and the two lines a follow-up defect. CLAUDE.md line 199 ('(Node 22 is needed)'), README.md line 233, .claude/agents/test-runner.md line 41 and .claude/agents/release-validator.md line 62 stay out: still true as 'Node 22', now inexact; default: ORCH opens a follow-up defect (the agent files are on the protected list; CLAUDE.md is owned by M0.10).

О7 — the form of the refusal. Default: Pixel Office keeps code 1 (SV-39 asserts it); each other command uses the code its help already gives for 'cannot run', or 1 where it has none, named in the design; the line is in Russian like the other messages of tools/ (for example «<команда>: нужен Node 22.23.4 или новее из линии 22 (сейчас 22.21.1). Подробности — tools/README.md»); the criteria check only: a code ≠ 0 (1 for Pixel Office), one stderr line with both versions, no stack. Today's Pixel Office text «нужен Node 22 (сейчас 22.21.1)» would be false for a refused 22.x, so it changes.

О8 — `--help` below the floor. Default: allowed — help writes nothing, and main.js prints its help before the version check today; the refusal criteria use working arguments (servers with --port 0 and so on). Alternative: refuse every start, help included.

О9 — a version that is not three whole numbers (`22.23`, `22.23.4.1`, `22.23.x`, `22.24.0-pre`, `x`, empty). Default (criterion 2): refused, never guessed (fail closed); official Node builds report three numbers, and a self-built `-pre` Node is refused with the same plain line.

О10 — the header canary of RT-4. The plan's seed (PLAN M0.9) names a Pixel Office server only; criterion 7 sharpens it to the team web and picker servers too (the diagnosis measured the same behaviour on them; each is a node:http server of tools/ reachable on 127.0.0.1) and to a head under 16 384 bytes (fact 5). Default: all three servers. Alternative: Pixel Office only, as the seed; the two other rows of criterion 7 then go by ORCH's record and a micro-amendment.

О11 — REQ-001 criterion 15 (status blocked) says the hook records an event «если Node 22 на компьютере есть»; after this work that means a Node 22 at or above the floor (a 22.21.1 alone is not enough). REQ-001 is not done, so AP-133 (an earlier done criterion) does not apply by its letter. Default: a WF-01 micro-amendment of REQ-001 criterion 15 in this run after the PASS of this block ('Node 22' → 'Node 22 at or above the floor of REQ-110'), not weaker; alternative: ORCH rules that the sentence of REQ-110's description is enough until REQ-001 is reworked. I did not touch REQ-001 (write set: the new block only).

The 'before' copy for docs/requirements.yaml. The tag base/ISS-0092-20261117-01 (6c756cd) holds a file of 13945 lines ending with REQ-107; the work file before this step held 14774 lines: REQ-108 and REQ-109 (M1SITE-20261117-01, REQ108AMEND-20261118-01), the REQ-103 amendments (REQ103AMEND-20261117-01) and the status edits of M0BACKLOG-20261028-01 step 04, all uncommitted. So `git diff base/ISS-0092-20261117-01 -- docs/requirements.yaml` shows those runs' edits as well as this block. The proof that this step changed only its block is the hash: the first 14774 lines after the write have the sha256 of the whole file before it (04a490e3…e98ebe), and the appended 251 lines equal the draft (cmp). REQ-VALIDATOR can repeat it with `head -n 14774 docs/requirements.yaml | shasum -a 256` and `tail -n +14775`.

The header probe of the plan (2 500 headers) needs a size bound to prove the count. Measured on Node 22.23.4 (trials D, D2): the count limit is 1 000 header lines in all (1 001 → 431), and a head over 16 384 bytes is refused by the size limit whatever the count (2 000 lines of 11 bytes, 22 920 bytes → 431). A probe with long lines would stay green under the mutant maxHeadersCount = 0 (with 2 500 short lines under the size limit that mutant gives 200, D2). The diagnosis's own probe was under the limit (15 048 bytes, its I13), so its finding stands; criterion 7 now says it in words, so the test cannot drift into a size probe.
